candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether merchant-booking growth and payment facilitation increase the need for third-party fraud, reconciliation, and supplier connectivity services.
candidates.next_evidence: Track 10-K/10-Q disclosures on merchant gross bookings, accommodation reservation revenue, payments, connected-trip investments, and supplier connectivity or platform risk disclosures.
candidates.node_relation: Obvious demand-side platform anchor; large OTA that depends on accommodation inventory distribution, merchant payments, supplier connectivity, fraud controls, and reservation workflows.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Online travel agency and travel reservation platforms
candidates.theme_relation: Consumer travel demand and online travel booking leader; useful reference for transaction volumes, merchant mix, accommodation demand, and connected-trip strategy.
candidates.why_include: Booking is the obvious public-market leader for online travel reservations and is a useful anchor for the downstream demand that flows into distribution, payments, and connectivity vendors.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Not underfollowed; included only as a reference/context anchor to avoid confusing supplier/back-office exposure with headline OTA exposure.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Whether SabreMosaic Marketplace growth, airline/hotel content wins, and post-divestiture deleveraging improve persistence of transaction revenue versus cyclicality in air travel volumes.
candidates.next_evidence: Review latest 10-Q booking volume trends, debt reduction after Hospitality Solutions sale, renewal rates, GDS regulation risks, and any disclosures on SabreMosaic adoption.
candidates.node_relation: Direct travel-distribution infrastructure provider through a B2B travel marketplace/GDS connecting travel suppliers and travel buyers; after the 2025 Hospitality Solutions divestiture, exposure is more concentrated in distribution and marketplace technology.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Travel technology, GDS, B2B travel marketplace
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order beneficiary of fragmented travel inventory that must be searched, priced, distributed, booked, and serviced across agencies, airlines, hotels, and other suppliers.
candidates.why_include: Sabre is one of the purest US-listed ways to express travel distribution and GDS exposure. Its revenue is tied to travel bookings and marketplace activity rather than owning hotels or planes.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It screens as a small-cap, leveraged travel-tech name rather than a clean software compounder, which may reduce generalist attention despite centrality to travel distribution workflows.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Large-chain PMS wins, implementation backlog, subscription mix, professional-services bottlenecks, and whether customer complexity creates durable switching costs.
candidates.next_evidence: Check FY2026 annual report, Marriott or other enterprise PMS deployments, subscription revenue growth, retention, implementation margins, and customer concentration.
candidates.node_relation: Direct hotel and resort back-office software provider; products include PMS, POS, inventory/procurement, payments-adjacent and guest-journey systems embedded in hospitality operations.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Hospitality software, property management systems, POS, inventory/procurement
candidates.theme_relation: Benefits from hotels, resorts, casinos, and hospitality operators modernizing fragmented property systems and integrating guest, booking, POS, and payment workflows.
candidates.why_include: Agilysys is a direct public hotel-software specialist with recurring revenue and property-system exposure. It fits the node better than broad enterprise software names because PMS/POS integration sits inside daily hotel operations.
candidates.why_underfollowed: It is often classified as small/mid-cap software rather than travel infrastructure; its relevance is operational and back-office rather than visible consumer travel demand.

candidates.hidden_signal_to_verify: Travel vertical revenue mix, enterprise travel client growth, take-rate stability, fraud/chargeback capabilities, and whether travel payments grow faster than the broader company.
candidates.next_evidence: Review latest 10-K/10-Q vertical revenue disclosures, travel ARR, payment volume by vertical, client wins, cross-border payment economics, and exposure to education concentration.
candidates.node_relation: Travel payments/back-office candidate; provides global payments enablement with explicit travel vertical exposure, including enterprise travel clients and cross-border payment workflows.
candidates.sector_or_industry: Vertical payments and payment enablement software
candidates.theme_relation: Second-order exposure to travel complexity through payment acceptance, reconciliation, cross-border flows, and client software integrations rather than direct travel inventory ownership.
candidates.why_include: Flywire is not a pure travel company, but travel payments are part of the target node and the company discloses travel vertical exposure. Its role may matter where travel merchants need high-value, cross-border, multi-currency payments and reconciliation.
candidates.why_underfollowed: Investor framing is often education/payments rather than travel-distribution infrastructure, so travel sensitivity may be hidden inside vertical payment disclosures.

evidence.claim: Booking Holdings disclosed that substantially all revenues are generated by online travel reservation services and that 70% of total gross bookings were generated on a merchant basis in 2025.

Sabre's 2025 10-K says the company provides global travel solutions through a B2B travel marketplace called Sabre Mosaic Marketplace and generates distribution revenue through transaction fees for bookings on its GDS.

Agilysys describes itself as a global provider of hospitality software and services, with customer use cases including PMS, POS, food and beverage inventory/procurement, and guest-facing hospitality systems.
evidence.source_title: Agilysys Announces Fiscal 2025 Fourth Quarter Record Revenue

evidence.claim: Agilysys FY2025 results disclosed annual recurring revenue of $170.1 million and subscription revenue growth of 39.5%, supporting the recurring-revenue and embedded-software angle.
evidence.source_title: Agilysys Announces Fiscal 2025 Fourth Quarter Record Revenue of $74.3M

evidence.claim: Flywire reported that 70% of Travel revenue was derived from large-scale enterprise institutions in 2025, indicating disclosed travel vertical exposure.
evidence.source_title: Flywire Reports Fourth Quarter and Fiscal-Year 2025 Financial Results

evidence.claim: PROS Holdings would be highly relevant to airline revenue management, but Thoma Bravo completed its acquisition in December 2025 and PROS became private, so it is not retained as a US-listed candidate.
evidence.source_title: Thoma Bravo Completes Acquisition of PROS Holdings, Inc.

memory_update.text: SABR is the purest US-listed underfollowed candidate for travel distribution/GDS exposure, but must be tested against leverage, GDS regulation, and transaction-volume cyclicality.
AGYS is a strong underfollowed hotel back-office software candidate due to PMS/POS/inventory integration and recurring revenue; verify enterprise deployments and implementation risk.
FLYW is a lower-purity but plausible travel-payments candidate; keep only if vertical disclosures show travel revenue and enterprise client growth remain material.
PROS Holdings should be removed from US-listed screens after the December 2025 Thoma Bravo take-private transaction, despite strong node relevance in airline revenue management.

node: Travel distribution, hotel connectivity, channel management, revenue management, and payments/fraud back office
summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for travel distribution and back-office connectivity. The reference lane is Booking Holdings as the obvious demand and platform anchor. The underfollowed lane is stronger in Sabre, Agilysys, and Flywire: Sabre is the purest listed GDS/travel marketplace exposure but carries leverage and travel-volume cyclicality; Agilysys is a hospitality software/PMS/POS specialist with recurring revenue and enterprise hotel/resort integrations; Flywire is a travel payments/back-office candidate with explicit travel vertical exposure but less pure because education remains a major vertical. PROS would have been highly relevant for airline revenue management, but evidence indicates it was acquired by Thoma Bravo and taken private in December 2025, so it is excluded from candidates.
